name: sidebar
description: A composable, themeable application sidebar for primary navigation with collapsible state, mobile overlay, and keyboard shortcut.

sidebar-menu-1.purpose: Primary nav item with icon — State × Type

_sidebar-badge.purpose: Notification count badge for nav items

menuType.note: Expand = full row (icon + label + badge + trailing). Collapse = icon-only, for collapsed sidebar mode.

logo.note: Branding slot — exempt from all token binding rules. Only size constraint applies. See agentic-design-system.md Branding Slots.

subMenuItem.note: Large left padding creates the visual indent communicating sub-item hierarchy.

tokens.iconRule: Icon Placeholder instances are stroke-based. Bind color on VECTOR node strokes — never on instance fill.

collapsible.offcanvas: Sidebar slides off-screen; full width when open
collapsible.icon: Collapses to icon-only strip — switch nav items to Type=Collapse

behavior.mobile: Renders as a full-screen overlay sheet on mobile with focus trap

composition.wrapper: SidebarProvider — required, owns state and keyboard shortcut
composition.logoSlot: 28×28px branding slot — replace with brand logomark. No token constraint on fill.
composition.navItemHierarchy: sidebar-menu-1 for primary items, _sidebar-menu-2 for sub-items. Never nest menu-1 inside menu-1.
composition.badgeUsage: _sidebar-badge for notification counts only — short numbers, not status labels

accessibility.mobile: Overlay sheet uses full focus trap on mobile

constraints: Always wrap in SidebarProvider — it owns collapse state and keyboard shortcut.
Logo fill is NOT token-bound — branding asset exempt from token rules. Size: 28×28px FIXED only.
Use color/sidebar/* tokens inside the sidebar only — they are scoped to this component.
Do not use color/sidebar/primary on badge — that token is for the logo block only. Use color/brand/primary.
Hover and Active states share the same token (color/sidebar/accent). Active persists on mouse-out.
Use sidebar-menu-1 Type=Collapse only when sidebar is in icon/collapsed mode.
Sub-items (_sidebar-menu-2) must always follow a parent sidebar-menu-1 — the indent implies hierarchy.
Do not use color/background/default/foreground for icon strokes inside sidebar — use color/sidebar/foreground.
color/sidebar/active is an undocumented token — use color/sidebar/accent instead.

useCases: Full application shells where primary navigation needs to be always accessible (dashboards, admin panels, SaaS apps)
Multi-section apps where users switch between major areas (Analytics, Settings, Users, Billing)
Workspaces with hierarchical navigation — top-level sections with nested sub-items below each
Apps that need icon-only collapsed mode on smaller screens to recover horizontal space
Mobile apps that render the sidebar as a slide-in overlay sheet
Applications requiring a persistent branding slot (logo + product name) anchored to the top of the nav

Type=Default.whenToUse: Standard app layout — sidebar is flush with the page edge, right border separates it from content

Type=Floating.whenToUse: Cards-based or elevated layout where the sidebar should feel like a panel rather than an edge element

Type=Inset.whenToUse: Sidebar is inset within the page layout — content wraps around it, creating a nested shell

State=Expanded.whenToUse: Default — full label and icon visible, all nav items readable
examples: Any app in its standard working state

State=Collapsed.whenToUse: Space is at a premium — show icons only

comparedTo.situation: Persistent full-app navigation with grouped sections, always visible or collapsible
Site-level top navigation with horizontal links and dropdown panels
A secondary page-level nav for sections within a single page
Collapsible content groups within a page (not navigation)

notes: color/sidebar/active was found in Figma and removed — renamed to color/sidebar/accent per docs.
Logo fill override removed — branding slot, not token-bound.
Hover and Active share color/sidebar/accent — distinction is behavioral (Active persists), not visual.

darkMode.notes: No known dark mode differences — all tokens are semantic and mode-aware.
